lead: Stenbolone (2-methyl-Δ1-dihydrotestosterone) is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid of the dihydrotestosterone (DHT) group, related to drostanolone, 1-testosterone and methylstenbolone. Like other anabolic-androgenic steroids it acts on the androgen receptor, the pathway through which compounds of this class are associated with greater muscle mass, which is the appearance-related reason such compounds interest people building a physique. Wikipedia states the compound itself was never marketed.[1]

Its 17β-acetate ester, stenbolone acetate, a prodrug, was sold as a depot intramuscular injection under names such as Anatrofin and Stenobolone.[1] A 1969 Mexican paper examined stenbolone acetate's effects on the normal ovary.[2]

Human data are limited to metabolism studies: after a single oral dose of the acetate to a volunteer, researchers identified nine urinary metabolites and detected the parent compound for more than 120 hours.[3] Equine anti-doping work includes it among screened anabolic steroids.[4]

angle.text: As a DHT-derived anabolic steroid, stenbolone belongs to the class of androgen-receptor agonists associated with muscle growth. Published human work on it concerns metabolism and detection rather than muscle or appearance outcomes, and the parent compound was never marketed.

paras: Stenbolone is an androgen receptor agonist.[1] The acetate is described as a prodrug, and the esterified form is given by depot intramuscular injection.[1] In a human metabolism study, only a small share of the dose (about 6.6 percent) was excreted as the parent compound, with most appearing as metabolites that were mainly conjugated to glucuronic acid, with only 16-hydroxylated isomers found in the sulfate fraction and no metabolites in the unconjugated fraction.[3] The nine metabolites included stenbolone itself, 3α-hydroxy derivatives, and 16-hydroxylated isomers.[3] Further urinary metabolites, including 18-hydroxylated forms, have been isolated from a single-dose study of mesterolone, methenolone and stenbolone.[5]

Wikipedia describes stenbolone as a synthetic androstane steroid and a DHT derivative, with formula C20H30O2, also called 2-methyl-Δ1-4,5α-dihydrotestosterone, and structurally related to drostanolone, 1-testosterone and methylstenbolone.[1] The acetate ester is 17β-acetoxy-2-methyl-5α-androst-1-en-3-one.[3]

As an anabolic steroid it is among compounds screened for in racehorse urine and relevant to sport anti-doping. A 2005 liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method for horse urine detected anabolic steroids that are poorly covered by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, noting that anabolic steroids are banned in the Olympic games and in horseracing and equestrian competitions.[4]
No studies found on muscle or appearance outcomes. The only human work identified concerns metabolism and one 1969 gynecological study of stenbolone acetate.[2][3][5]

timeline.event: Study of stenbolone acetate's effects on the normal ovary published.[2]
Urinary metabolites of stenbolone acetate characterised in a human volunteer.[3]
18-hydroxylated metabolites of mesterolone, methenolone and stenbolone isolated from human urine.[5]
LC-MS/MS screening method for anabolic steroids in horse urine published.[4]

name: Stenbolone

card.summary: A DHT-derived anabolic steroid whose acetate ester was an old injectable; known today mostly from metabolism studies.

quick.overview:
Stenbolone is a DHT-derived anabolic steroid. Only its acetate ester was ever sold, as an injectable.
The human literature is thin and mostly concerns metabolism and detection.
quick.mechanism: It acts as an androgen receptor agonist; the acetate ester serves as a depot prodrug.
quick.risks: No clinical safety data were found beyond its classification as an anabolic steroid.
